sections.title: Neck Pain Treatment in Downtown Austin

paras.t: Stiff in the morning, tight by mid-afternoon, and it's starting to run into your shoulders. Casey Morgan D.C. finds what's causing it before he treats it.

bullets.text: In and out in minutes, not rushed

sections.name: What Section
sections.title: Neck pain rarely stays in the neck

paras.t: It might start as stiffness when you turn your head. Then it's a knot between your shoulder blades, a headache by Thursday, or tingling that runs down into your arm.
Most of the neck pain Dr. Morgan sees comes from the same place: long days sitting, looking down at a screen, and a neck that's been working harder than it should for years.
Numbness, tingling, or weakness in your arms or hands count. They can mean a nerve in your neck is involved. Tell Dr. Morgan even if they don't hurt.

sections.name: What Section
sections.title: What we usually find on a neck X-ray

paras.t: A healthy neck has a gentle curve. In a lot of people who sit all day, that curve has started to straighten out, the head has shifted forward, and the discs between the bones are starting to thin.
None of that happens overnight, which is why a neck that's been "a little tight" for years can suddenly start to really hurt.

callouts.title: This is why we image before we treat.
callouts.text: Dr. Morgan takes digital X-rays on site when your exam calls for them, reads them himself, and shows them to you the same visit.

sections.title: Find it, fix it, keep it from coming back

paras.t: When we'd send you for an MRI. If you haven't improved after about six weeks, or you finish a plan with less change than expected, Dr. Morgan will refer you for one.

bullets.body: A full history and exam: how your neck moves, where it hurts and where it doesn't, and whether anything runs into your shoulders or arms. Digital X-rays if your exam calls for them.
Chiropractic adjustments, and spinal decompression when a disc is involved. Dr. Morgan starts gentle with the neck, especially on the first visit.
Once the problem is corrected, most patients move to maintenance, about once every two weeks. Some stop entirely.

sections.name: First Visit Section
sections.title: Your first visit, start to finish

paras.t: First visit runs about 30 minutes. After that, most visits take a few minutes. Dr. Morgan built the practice around working people.

steps.title: We find out what is actually happening
steps.text: Full history and exam. What hurts, what you have already tried, what you want to get back to doing. Any necessary digital X-rays, taken on site.

steps.title: Dr. Morgan shows you the imaging, same day
steps.text: He marks it up and walks you through it right there. You will see what he sees. Most patients get their first adjustment the same visit.

steps.title: You come back for the full report
steps.text: Within a few days, Dr. Morgan lays out what he found and exactly what he recommends. What it will take, how long, and what it costs. Then you decide.

sections.name: What Section
sections.title: How long until this actually feels better

paras.t: Most people want a number before they start. Dr. Morgan will give you one, just not before he has examined you and looked at your imaging. He will not guess.
What he can tell you up front is how it usually goes, including the part most offices skip: the first two weeks are uneven.
If you are only trying to get out of pain, a shorter plan can do that. If you want it to stay fixed, it takes about 90 days. Dr. Morgan will give you both options and let you pick.

tags.text: Inconsistent, and that's normal. You'll have a good day and think it's fixed, then a bad one and think it's not working. Dr. Morgan warns you about this on day one. Real change usually starts around the end of week two, and better sleep is often the first thing people notice.

The bulk of the plan. A typical plan is about 24 visits over 90 days, two to three times a week at the start, then less often as you improve. Some people need fewer. Dr. Morgan checks your progress along the way.
Most patients move to maintenance, about once every two weeks. Some stop entirely. Dr. Morgan will tell you when you're there.

faqs.q: I'm nervous about getting my neck adjusted. Do I have to?
faqs.a: No. Tell Dr. Morgan, and he'll explain exactly what he wants to do before he does it. He starts gentle on the first visit, and if you'd rather not have your neck adjusted, he'll work around it. A lot of first-time patients say the same thing, and most are surprised how easy it is.
No. Most people describe it as relief. You might hear a pop, which is gas releasing from the joint, not bones cracking.

faqs.q: Why does my neck pain cause headaches?
faqs.a: The muscles and joints at the top of your neck refer pain up into the head. When those are tight or not moving well, a headache often follows.
Only if your exam calls for it. If Dr. Morgan takes them, they happen on site at your first visit, with no separate appointment or bill.

faqs.q: How many visits will I need?
faqs.a: Dr. Morgan won't know until he's examined you. A typical plan is about 24 visits over 90 days, two to three times a week at the start. He gives you a real recommendation on your second visit.

faqs.q: When should I go to the ER instead?
faqs.a: If your neck pain comes with a fever and a stiff neck, the worst headache of your life, or new numbness or weakness after a fall or crash, go to an emergency room.
